title: Evaluating Generate–Validate–Repair Pipelines for Intent‑to‑Configuration NetOps Tasks: A Preregistered Paired Study
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study comparing a baseline single‑shot LLM configuration generator against a guarded generate→validate→repair pipeline (including a canary stage) on a 1,000‑task synthetic NetOps stress corpus (2,000 paired episodes). The declared model was gpt‑5‑mini (provider: openai_responses) and validation used a deterministic digital‑twin validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5). Under preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics exactly one sampled initial generation per task was deterministically reused by both arms; downstream validation and the permitted single repair call (guarded arm only) are therefore the only mechanisms that can create paired outcome differences. Observed outcomes: baseline safe‑deploy = 995/1000 = 0.995; guarded safe‑deploy = 1000/1000 = 1.000; paired difference = 0.005 (n11=995, n10=5, n01=0, n00=0). The preregistered confirmatory test (exact two‑sided McNemar) yields p = 0.0625 (not < 0.05). A preregistered paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) is [0.001, 0.01] and is reported as a descriptive summary. Only five validator‑triggered repairs occurred and total hosted model calls used = 1005 (shared_initial = 1000; repair = 5). We report the exact McNemar outcome as the prespecified confirmatory result, label any one‑sided McNemar as exploratory/post‑hoc, and interpret the small absolute guarded benefit in light of sparse discordant counts, near‑unity baseline validity, validator scope, and the shared_initial_candidate design.

sections.introduction:
Automating intent→configuration translation for network operations (NetOps) promises reduced manual effort but raises safety risks: incorrect sequencing, transient invariant violations, and unintended interference with protected fields can convert plausible command sequences into harmful actions. Prior surveys and controlled studies document frequent LLM hallucinations, prompt sensitivity, and structured‑output failures in code and configuration generation, motivating guarded architectures that pair generative models with deterministic validators and bounded repair procedures [1],[2].

We study, under a frozen preregistration, the incremental effect of a downstream deterministic validator plus a single permitted repair call when baseline and guarded conditions reuse the same sampled initial candidate (generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate). This design isolates the downstream intervention (validation and at‑most‑one repair) so any paired difference is attributable to those mechanisms rather than to first‑pass generation differences, prompt engineering, or sampling variance.

Our contributions are: (1) a preregistered paired experiment (Npairs = 1000) using a deterministic selection rule from the challenging_workflow_stress_v1 synthetic corpus and a deterministic digital‑twin validator; (2) full artifact‑grounded execution accounting showing completed_pairs = 1000, hosted_model_call_event_count = 1005, and repair calls = 5; and (3) transparent confirmatory reporting: the preregistered exact two‑sided McNemar did not reach α = 0.05 (p = 0.0625), with the bootstrap CI reported as a preregistered descriptive summary (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729). We explicitly note that execution/model_configuration.json records temperature = null/unset; null/unset is not evidence of deterministic hosted‑model sampling and does not imply temperature = 0.
sections.related_work:
Empirical and survey literature establishes (i) that LLMs produce frequent hallucinations and are sensitive to prompt phrasing, which impairs correctness for structured tasks including code and configuration generation [2],[7]; (ii) that constrained decoding and schema‑aware planning reduce syntactic and executable errors in structured domains, though much evidence originates outside NetOps and relies on validator/tool fidelity when transferred [3]; and (iii) that agentic NetOps architectures emphasizing verifier‑assisted repair, protocol‑mediated execution, and proof‑carrying audit traces are proposed mitigations but lack broad production‑scale validation across heterogeneous networks [4],[5],[6].

This study complements those works by preregistering a paired estimand that explicitly holds the initial sampled candidate constant across conditions. Under shared_initial_candidate semantics, downstream validation and permitted repair are the only sources of paired differences; thus our findings isolate what deterministic validator+repair layers can contribute independently of first‑pass generation improvements.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and design fidelity. The experiment was preregistered as cand‑003‑stud‑001 and frozen before any hosted‑model calls; the preregistration SHA‑256 is recorded in the execution manifest (ab4c6436c6ece56bf47da7730d50485a17cdb9bb86a90a4231042303d3b489ec). Key predeclared elements: paired binary design, task_count = 1000, deterministic task selection using the challenging_workflow_stress_v1 profile, generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate (one sampled initial generation per task reused across arms), initial_generation_calls_per_task = 1, maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1, primary estimand = paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline, and primary test = exact two‑sided McNemar. The analysis executor and result schema (paired_binary_analysis_v1; paired_binary_episode_v1) were preregistered and executed without human adjudication.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics and interpretive consequences. Because both arms reuse the exact same sampled initial candidate for each task, any paired outcome difference can only arise from deterministic validator decisions and the single allowed repair call in the guarded arm. The design therefore does not measure effects that would arise from independent first‑pass generations, alternative prompts, constrained decoding, or stochastic sampling differences; those interventions were not executed and are outside this estimand.

Model and validator configuration. The declared model is gpt‑5‑mini (provider: openai_responses) and the runtime configuration recorded max_output_tokens = 2000 and temperature = null/unset in execution/model_configuration.json (null/unset is explicitly not evidence of deterministic sampling). Orchestration used adapter_family = hosted_netops_gvr_v1 and validation used deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (validator version 5.0). The validator implements the task manifest policies (required_sequence checks, protected‑field constraints, and final_group/minimum_active constraints) via a deterministic digital‑twin emulator and emits structured validator traces and a binary safe‑deploy verdict per episode.

Task corpus, selection, and scoring. Tasks are synthetic NetOps intents with initial_state, expected_final_state, required_sequence, allowed_touched_fields, and difficulty labels (very_hard, extreme). The preregistered deterministic selection rule produced exactly 1000 unique task indices. Scoring used scoring_rule = full_intent_constraint_validation producing a binary score (valid/invalid) required by the paired analysis. The preregistration specified missingness and failure treatments; the primary analysis used 'complete_pair_primary' and prespecified sensitivity analyses (failure-as-zero) if needed.

Execution constraints and accounting. The adapter limited model calls per the preregistration (initial_generation_calls_per_task = 1; maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1). Retries were constrained (maximum_attempts_per_call = 1). All seeds, selection rules, and analysis scripts were fixed before model invocation.
sections.results:
Execution summary and artifact accounting. The run executed 2,000 episodes (shared_initial + guarded/baseline pairs) and completed without failed episodes. Provider audit (deterministic_reconciliation.json) reports hosted_model_call_event_count = 1005, with stage_counts = {shared_initial_generation = 1000, repair = 5}. All deterministic consistency checks passed and contamination checks found no prompt‑leakage flags.

Primary paired outcomes and preregistered test. The 2×2 paired contingency table (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv) is: n11 = 995 (both succeeded), n10 = 5 (guarded succeeded, baseline failed), n01 = 0 (baseline succeeded, guarded failed), n00 = 0 (both failed). Observed success rates are baseline = 995/1000 = 0.995 and guarded = 1000/1000 = 1.000; the observed paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.005. The preregistered confirmatory test (exact two‑sided McNemar) returns p = 0.0625; this does not meet the preregistered two‑sided α = 0.05 threshold and therefore the preregistered H1 is not supported.

Preregistered descriptive summaries and inferential hierarchy. The preregistered paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, bootstrap_seed = 1729) yields [0.001, 0.01] and is presented as a secondary descriptive summary (artifact: analysis/analysis_log.jsonl). We emphasize the preregistered inferential hierarchy: the exact two‑sided McNemar test is the prespecified confirmatory analysis and it did not reach α = 0.05 (p = 0.0625); the bootstrap CI and any one‑sided McNemar reported below are descriptive or exploratory only and do not overturn the preregistered confirmatory conclusion. The bootstrap CI excludes zero because bootstrap percentile intervals can produce nonzero bounds when discordant counts are extremely sparse (here n10=5, n01=0); this behavior is a statistical artifact of resampling discrete paired outcomes and is sensitive to the small number of discordant pairs.

Exploratory / archive‑grounded diagnostics. A one‑sided McNemar (guarded > baseline) computed post‑hoc yields p = 0.03125; because a one‑sided test was not prespecified in the frozen preregistration it is labeled exploratory. Only five validator‑triggered repairs occurred (repair stage_count = 5) and representative episode artifacts show repairs addressing required_sequence violations or protected‑field touches; repaired candidates passed revalidation in archived validator traces. Total hosted model calls used = 1005 (shared_initial = 1000; repair = 5). Contamination_summary.csv is empty and missingness_summary.csv records zero failed or unscorable episodes.
sections.discussion:
Confirmatory result and power reconciliation. The preregistered primary inference (exact two‑sided McNemar) did not reach significance at α = 0.05 (p = 0.0625). This null confirmatory outcome must be interpreted alongside the preregistered power_and_precision_plan: the plan assumed baseline ≈ 0.60 and targeted an absolute increase of 0.15 for adequate power. The observed baseline (0.995) is far higher than planned, producing very few discordant pairs and substantially reducing sensitivity for the preregistered two‑sided test. Thus the study's failure to reject at α = 0.05 reflects a combination of a small absolute effect and sparse discordant counts under near‑unity baseline validity rather than strong evidence of no possible practical guarded benefit in other regimes with higher baseline failure prevalence.

Mechanistic interpretation under shared_initial_candidate semantics. Because both arms began from the identical sampled candidate, observed paired gains can only result from deterministic validator decisions and the single allowed repair call. The five observed repairs demonstrate that a deterministic validator with appropriate coverage can correct certain ordering or protected‑field violations. However, the low repair invocation count constrains general statements about repair efficacy across diverse failure modes; it may reflect the synthetic corpus, generator behavior for the declared model, or limited validator coverage. Distinguishing among these causes requires targeted follow‑ups that vary generation semantics, repair budgets, and validator rule sets.

Threats to validity and externality. Construct validity depends on the rule coverage of deterministic_netops_validator_v5: omitted semantic or emergent multi‑device policy checks would inflate measured success. Internal validity benefits from deterministic seeding, preregistered missingness treatments, and zero failed episodes; nonetheless, shared_initial_candidate semantics intentionally exclude measurement of first‑pass generation improvements. External validity is limited by the single declared model (gpt‑5‑mini) and the synthetic task corpus; results do not generalize automatically to heterogeneous vendor/legacy production environments or to other model families. Conclusion validity is limited by the sparse discordant counts that reduce power for exact paired tests in regimes with near‑unity baseline success.

Operational implications and recommended preregistered follow‑ups. Artifact‑grounded results indicate that validator‑guided repair can avert some unsafe outcomes in synthetic workflows, but measurable marginal gains depend on baseline failure prevalence, validator sensitivity/coverage, and permitted repair budget. Recommended preregistered follow‑ups (supported by the archived run and its artifacts) are: (1) run an independent first‑pass generation arm (no shared_initial_candidate) to measure prompt/decoding effects; (2) sweep repair budgets (0..k repairs) to quantify marginal returns per failure class; (3) expand validator rule suites and topology heterogeneity to probe external validity; and (4) evaluate multiple model families to map model dependence. Each follow‑up should align power calculations to expected baseline failure rates and preregister confirmatory analyses.
sections.conclusion:
In a preregistered paired study that held initial sampled candidates constant across arms (shared_initial_candidate semantics) on a 1,000‑task synthetic NetOps stress corpus, a guarded generate→validate→repair pipeline produced a small absolute paired improvement (0.005) compared with a baseline single‑shot generator; the preregistered exact two‑sided McNemar confirmatory test did not reach α = 0.05 (p = 0.0625). Only five validator repairs were invoked and hosted model calls used = 1005. The primary prespecified inference is the exact McNemar result; secondary descriptive summaries (paired bootstrap CI = [0.001, 0.01], 10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) are reported as preregistered descriptive statistics and a one‑sided McNemar is explicitly labeled exploratory because it was not prespecified. These artifact‑grounded results show that deterministic validator+repair safeguards can prevent some unsafe outcomes under the tested conditions, but the measurable marginal gains are constrained when baseline outputs are already highly valid and when the paired design isolates downstream effects. The archived preregistration, raw responses, validator traces, and analysis artifacts are available in the run evidence bundle to enable replication and preregistered follow‑ups.

[3] S. Banjade, "Schema‑Constrained LLM Planning for Executable Molecular Workflows: An Intent‑to‑Execution Infrastructure for Cheminformatics," ChemRxiv, 2026. doi: 10.26434/chemrxiv.15005091/v1.

[4] A. Harrison, "Protocol‑Mediated Execution Governance for LLM Agent Systems," SSRN, 2026. doi: 10.2139/ssrn.6426760.

[5] J. Augé et al., "Aether: Network Validation Using Agentic AI and Digital Twin," arXiv:2604.18233, 2026. [Online]. Available: https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.18233

Preregistration: cand‑003‑stud‑001 (frozen prior to any model calls; preregistration SHA‑256 recorded in the execution manifest = ab4c6436c6ece56bf47da7730d50485a17cdb9bb86a90a4231042303d3b489ec). Research‑director constraint before autonomy lock: topic family limited to “Generative AI and LLMs for NetOps.” Immutable initial master prompt archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA‑256 = 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). After the autonomy lock, literature review, preregistration finalization, execution, analysis, manuscript drafting, autonomous peer review, and automated revisions were performed by the autonomous research run; no human manually edited the manuscript technical content after the autonomy lock.
limitations: Single‑model scope: only the declared model gpt‑5‑mini was evaluated; results do not generalize across model families or versions.

Synthetic corpus and deterministic validator: tasks come from a synthetic stress corpus and validation used a deterministic digital twin (deterministic_netops_validator_v5); external validity to heterogeneous vendor/legacy environments is limited.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics: the paired comparison isolates downstream validator/repair effects only; it does not measure differences that would arise from independent first‑pass generations or alternative prompting arms that were not executed (those arms were not part of the frozen preregistration).

Low baseline failure prevalence: baseline success = 99.5%; the preregistered power plan assumed baseline≈0.60 and a target effect of 0.15, so the observed baseline greatly reduces sensitivity to detect small absolute gains. This mismatch is reported explicitly and reduces the study's ability to detect very small practical effects using the preregistered confirmatory test.
Sparse repairs and interpretation limits: only five validator repairs were invoked, constraining inference about repair efficacy across failure modes.

Statistical nuance: the preregistered primary test is exact two‑sided McNemar (p = 0.0625). The paired bootstrap percentile CI [0.001, 0.01] is a preregistered descriptive summary but is sensitive to sparse discordant counts; a one‑sided McNemar (p = 0.03125) was computed post‑hoc and is explicitly labeled exploratory because it was not prespecified in the frozen preregistration.

Construct validity: the safe‑deploy binary depends on the emulator/validator's rule set; semantic and emergent multi‑device policy violations may be underrepresented in the validator's modeled constraints.
